target: 가랑비에 옷 젖는 줄 모른다더니, 자잘한 지출이 쌓여 이달 카드값이 어마어마했다.
english: You don't notice the drizzle soaking your clothes—little expenses piled up into a huge card bill this month.
tip: 가랑비에 옷 젖다 (garangbie ot jeotda = drizzle soaks clothes) = small things pile up unnoticed.

target: 시작이 반이라니, 일단 부담 없이 첫 문장이라도 써 보자.
english: Starting is half the battle, so let's just write the first sentence without pressure.
tip: 시작이 반이다 (sijagi banida = the start is half) = getting started is the hardest part.

target: 여행 일정에 저마다 참견하니 사공이 많으면 배가 산으로 간다고, 결국 아무 데도 못 정했다.
english: With everyone butting into the itinerary—too many boatmen steer the boat up a mountain—we ended up deciding on nowhere.
tip: 사공이 많으면 배가 산으로 간다 (sagongi maneumyeon baega saneuro ganda) = too many cooks spoil the broth.

target: 벼는 익을수록 고개를 숙인다고, 진짜 대가일수록 오히려 더 겸손했다.
english: The riper the rice, the lower it bows its head—the true masters were, if anything, the humblest.
tip: 벼는 익을수록 고개를 숙인다 (byeoneun igeulsurok gogaereul suginda) = the wiser one grows, the humbler.

target: 합격 발표도 안 났는데 벌써 이사 갈 집부터 알아보다니, 김칫국부터 마시는구나.
english: The results aren't even out and you're already house-hunting—you're drinking the kimchi broth first.
tip: 김칫국부터 마신다 (gimchitgukbuteo masinda = drinking the broth first) = counting chickens before they hatch.

target: 모처럼 유명한 절을 찾았더니 하필 공사 중이라, 가는 날이 장날이었다.
english: I finally visited the famous temple only to find it under construction—the very day I went was market day.
tip: 가는 날이 장날 (ganeun nari jangnal = the day you go is market day) = an unlucky coincidence.

target: 대출로 급한 불은 껐지만, 근본 대책이 없으니 언 발에 오줌 누기에 불과했다.
english: The loan put out the immediate fire, but with no real fix it was just peeing on frozen feet.
tip: 언 발에 오줌 누기 (eon bare ojum nugi = peeing on frozen feet) = a stopgap that soon backfires.

target: 요즘은 신입을 정규직으로 뽑는 일이 가뭄에 콩 나듯 드물다.
english: These days hiring a newcomer as a full-time employee is as rare as beans sprouting in a drought.
tip: 가뭄에 콩 나듯 (gamume kong nadeut = like beans in a drought) = very rare, few and far between.

target: 인생사 새옹지마라고, 지금의 불운이 훗날 복이 될지 누가 알겠는가.
english: Life is a blessing in disguise—who knows if today's misfortune becomes tomorrow's fortune.
tip: 새옹지마 (saeongjima) is 'the frontier old man's horse': it ran off (bad), came back with another (good), his son fell off it (bad). Fortune keeps flipping – the whole saying in four syllables.

target: 유비무환이라고, 서버 장애에 대비해 백업 체계부터 든든히 갖춰 두었다.
english: Preparedness averts calamity—we set up a solid backup system in case of server failure.
tip: 유비무환 (yubimuhwan, 有備無患) = with preparation, there is no worry.

target: 출장 가는 김에 오랜 친구까지 만나고 오니 그야말로 일석이조였다.
english: Meeting an old friend on the same business trip really was killing two birds with one stone.
tip: 일석이조 (ilseogijo, 一石二鳥) = one stone, two birds.

target: 숙소는 전망도 좋은데 조식까지 훌륭하니 그야말로 금상첨화였다.
english: The lodging had a great view and excellent breakfast to boot—truly the icing on the cake.
tip: 금상첨화 (geumsangcheomhwa, 錦上添花) = flowers added to brocade; a welcome bonus.

target: 비행기가 세 시간이나 연착된 데다, 설상가상으로 부친 짐까지 사라져 버렸다.
english: The flight was delayed three hours and, to make matters worse, my checked luggage vanished too.
tip: 설상가상 (seolsanggasang, 雪上加霜) = frost on top of snow; troubles pile up.

target: 대기만성이라더니, 그는 마흔이 넘어서야 비로소 인정받는 작가가 되었다.
english: A great vessel is completed late—he became a recognized writer only after turning forty.
tip: 대기만성 (daegimanseong, 大器晩成) = a great talent matures slowly.

target: 자금은 바닥나고 투자자마저 등을 돌려, 회사는 그야말로 사면초가에 몰렸다.
english: Funds gone and even the investors turning their backs, the company was truly besieged on all sides.
tip: 사면초가 (samyeonchoga, 四面楚歌) = surrounded on all sides with no way out.

target: 그렇게 싼 항공권이 진짜일까 반신반의하면서도 결국 결제 버튼을 눌렀다.
english: Half-doubting such a cheap airfare could be real, I still ended up hitting the pay button.
tip: 반신반의 (bansinbanui, 半信半疑) = half-believing, half-doubting.

target: 천고마비의 계절이니 단풍 구경 삼아 훌쩍 여행을 떠나기에 그만이다.
english: It's the crisp, high-sky season, perfect for taking off on a spur-of-the-moment foliage trip.
tip: 천고마비 (cheongomabi) is literally 'sky high, horses fat' – autumn air is clear and the harvest fattens the horses. Four syllables that mean the perfect crisp season.

target: 그는 업계에서 발이 넓어 어지간한 사람은 다 알고 지낸다.
english: He's so well-connected in the industry that he knows just about everyone.
tip: 발이 넓다 (bari neolda = feet are wide) = to be well-connected.

target: 언니는 눈이 높아서 웬만한 상대는 도무지 성에 차지 않는 모양이다.
english: My older sister has such high standards that ordinary suitors just won't do.
tip: 눈이 높다 (nuni nopda = eyes are high) = to have high standards.

target: 할머니는 손이 커서 명절이면 온 동네가 먹고도 남을 만큼 음식을 하신다.
english: Grandma is so generous that on holidays she makes more than enough food to feed the whole neighborhood.
tip: 손이 크다 (soni keuda = hands are big) = to be generous and lavish.

target: 그 팀장은 입이 무거워 은밀한 고민을 털어놓기에 마음이 놓인다.
english: That manager is so tight-lipped that it's a relief to confide private worries in him.
tip: 입이 무겁다 (ibi mugeopda = mouth is heavy) = discreet, keeps secrets.

target: 남편은 귀가 얇아서 광고만 봤다 하면 필요도 없는 물건을 덜컥 사 온다.
english: My husband is so easily swayed that the moment he sees an ad he buys things we don't even need.
tip: 귀가 얇다 (gwiga yalda = ears are thin) = easily persuaded.

target: 이번 면접에서도 미역국을 먹었다며 동생이 잔뜩 풀이 죽어 있었다.
english: My younger sibling was thoroughly crestfallen, saying he'd flunked this interview too.
tip: 미역국을 먹다 (miyeokgugeul meokda = to eat seaweed soup) = to fail an exam or interview.

target: 도대체 언제 국수를 먹여 줄 거냐고 친척들이 만날 때마다 성화다.
english: The relatives pester me at every gathering about when on earth I'll finally get married.
tip: 국수를 먹다 (guksureul meokda = to eat noodles) = to get married.

target: 마감이 코앞에 닥쳐서야 이제 발등에 불이 떨어진 듯 부랴부랴 일에 매달렸다.
english: Only with the deadline right on top of me did I scramble at the work as if a fire had landed on my feet.
tip: 발등에 불이 떨어지다 (baldeunge buri tteoreojida = fire lands on your feet) = a sudden, pressing crisis.

target: 온종일 골목골목을 걸어 다녔더니 숙소에 도착할 즈음엔 완전히 파김치가 됐다.
english: After walking alley to alley all day, I was utterly wilted by the time I reached the lodging.
tip: 파김치가 되다 (pagimchiga doeda = to become limp scallion kimchi) = to be worn out.

target: 이번 손실은 지난번에 입은 손해에 비하면 새 발의 피에 불과하다.
english: This loss is a mere drop in the bucket compared with the damage we took last time.
tip: 새 발의 피 (sae barui pi = a bird's-foot of blood) = a trivial, tiny amount.

target: 말도 안 통하는 오지로 혼자 배낭여행을 떠나다니, 간이 커도 보통 큰 게 아니다.
english: Backpacking off alone to a remote place where you can't even communicate—that takes some serious nerve.
tip: 간이 크다 (gani keuda = liver is big) = bold, daring.

target: 새로 팀을 이끌게 되니 막중한 책임감에 어깨가 무겁다.
english: Now that I've been put in charge of a team, the heavy responsibility weighs on my shoulders.
tip: 어깨가 무겁다 (eokkaega mugeopda = shoulders are heavy) = to feel burdened by responsibility.

target: 막내가 입이 짧아 낯선 음식은 좀처럼 손도 대지 않으려 한다.
english: My youngest is such a picky eater that he'll hardly even touch unfamiliar food.
tip: 입이 짧다 (ibi jjalda = mouth is short) = to be a picky eater.
